_note: PostgreSQL rules that sql_tree.js does not have yet (F42, worker f42-pg). Each vector gives the members of a tree summary that the right tree has. The test runs them as todo: it does not fail, and it shows a pass as soon as the rule exists.

vectors.name: data_modifying_cte_is_a_subquery
vectors.reason: the body of a CTE that starts with DELETE, INSERT or UPDATE is a plain paren, not a subquery with a query
vectors.text: WITH d AS (DELETE FROM t RETURNING *) SELECT * FROM d

vectors.name: rows_from_is_not_a_clause
vectors.reason: the FROM of ROWS FROM (...) opens a second FROM clause
vectors.text: SELECT * FROM ROWS FROM (f(1), g(2)) AS r(a,b)

vectors.name: update_has_set_and_returning
vectors.reason: UPDATE has the clause WHERE only: SET and RETURNING are not clause words of the dialect table
vectors.text: UPDATE t SET a = 1 WHERE b = 2 RETURNING a

vectors.name: insert_has_values_and_returning
vectors.reason: INSERT has no clause: VALUES, ON CONFLICT and RETURNING are not clause words of the dialect table
vectors.text: INSERT INTO t (a) VALUES (1) ON CONFLICT (a) DO NOTHING RETURNING a
